newsitem.title: USA: Dataquest sees personal computer market growing.
newsitem.headline: Dataquest sees personal computer market growing.

text.p: The personal computer market is expected to grow 19 percent this year, with shipments surpassing 84.3 million units, market research firm Dataquest said Tuesday.
The company also said the market will continue to post double-digit growth through the year 2001 with shipments reaching 151.6 million units.

"The PC war between Dell (Computer Corp.) and the other vendors will change the industry landscape forever," said Bill Schaub, Dataquest's computer group director. "Everyone dependent upon the PC industry needs to navigate this new terrain very carefully."
To emulate Dell's growth, many of the company's rivals are looking at adopting its lower-cost model of selling PCs directly to customers.

Compaq Computer Corp., for example, plans to start making PCs to order in addition to its current manufacturing practices, but it will also keep selling PCs through distributors and retail outlets. Two weeks ago, Packard Bell NEC announced it will begin selling some of its PCs directly to business customers.
Dataquest, a subsidiary of the Gartner Group, said the challenge is for PC manufacturers to accelerate inventory turnover and increase their return on investment.
